title: Speech of President Arroyo during the Jobs Forum on Overseas Employment
text:
Speech of Her Excellency Gloria Macapagal-Arroyo President of the Philippines During the Jobs Forum on Overseas Employment

[Delivered at the Heroes Hall, Malacañang, March 2, 2009]

Maraming salamat, Secretary Marianito Roque sa iyong pagpakilala sa akin.

Secretary Boboy Syjuco, ang chairman ng TESDA; ang ating ibang mga opisyal ng DOLE; yung ating mga stakeholders; yung ating mga presentors: si Lita Hizon for the land-based and Marlon Roño for sea-based recruiters; lahat ng mga iba’t-ibang mga sektor na interesado, lalo na yung mga manggagawa:

Thank you all for coming.

I called for this second round of the job summit to focus on overseas employment. And I’m very glad to hear from the report of Undersecretary Padilla that there are 500,000 jobs available abroad because we have lost about 5,000 jobs. So for every worker who has lost his or her job, 100 are waiting depending on the skills.

In this second round, people on the ground, like labor attaches and welfare officers have been invited. I asked for at least one for Asia — saan ang ating labor attaché o welfare officer mula sa Asia? — okey, very good, thank you. (applause) For the Middle East — saan yung taga-Middle East natin? — very good, yes. (Applause) Saudi and Al Khobar, okey. Siyempre kasi Saudi has 1.5 million of our 8 million people abroad. Europe, (applause) Geneva and Americas (applause) from Canada. We invited them, instead of only the officials of the head office of the DOLE. Kasi kailangan marinig ang boses ng mga nandoon sa mga nasusugatan at nakikibaka.

And I have often said that in recent months, we were lucky to be less battered than others during the initial surge of the global economic crisis, because we have worked hard to be lucky. Years earlier, we decided to swallow the bitter pill of reforms that later fortified our economic fundamentals and gave us financial space to do all the things we need to do now in order to ease the burden on our workers losing their jobs. We raised revenues; we cracked down on smugglers; we reformed our tax collection system, our banking laws and practices. We borrowed sparingly, we brought down our foreign debts and we spent prudently, even as we moved fast to improve our human and physical infrastructure, lalo na ang ating human infrastructure na kailangang-kailangan ngayon.

The result of our tough choices is evident. Yung sinabi ni Undersecretary Padilla na 500,000 jobs are available – well, dito sa Pilipinas yung Grant Thornton Business Survey, that I think our Cabinet members should disseminate, reports that many Philippine companies will hire more people and raise pay despite the global slowdown. So the challenge is to match jobs with skills. So malaki ang papel ni Boboy Syjuco dito sa hamon na ito. Kaya kanina pinag-uusapan natin, at doon kay Boboy, kung gaano kalaki ang hamon niya dahil sa report na nandoon yung trabaho, ang problema or ang hamon, yung matching.

Eh kasi si Nitoy isang career official, matagal na matagal na siya nasa gobyerno. So Nitoy sabi ko, di ba di hamak ang laki ng budget natin sa TESDA hambing sa noong araw? ‘Di ba noong araw budget sa TESDA 100 million, 200 million? Sabi ni Nitoy, “80 million pa nga,” eh sabi niya. So 80 million, 100 million, 200 million. Tapos nung pumasok yata tayo ginawa nating half a billion, tapos ginawa nating one billion. Ngayon ay two billion ang budget ng TESDA. (Applause) At sabi ko kay Boboy, “at huwag kang mag-alala, don’t try to have to live within two billion kung kailangan. Kasi kung maubos mo yang two billion eh di meron tayong policy sa pamahalaan ngayon sa mga ahensya — use it or lose it. So kung maubos mo yung two billion sa pangangailangan to match the skills, aba yung mga ibang medyo makupad na maggamit ng kanilang… yung mahinang absorptive capacity na ahensya, eh di yun ang babawasan natin ng budge,t at ililipat natin ang budget nila sa DOLE at saka sa TESDA.” (Applause)

So the message is, let us join hands against the global crisis. Let us join hands now to prevent the world crisis from becoming a Philippine crisis. Let us join hands to make sure that we stay on track towards sustainable growth. Kaya sa inyong lahat, mabuhay! Maraming salamat.

Di na kailangan ng maraming salita. Ang importante ay magtrabaho tayong lahat.

Thank you. (Applause)
